$note: Every PERMITTED foreground/background combination, declared explicitly. A pair not listed here is not an approved combination. Specs are dotted paths into design-system/dist/tokens.json; because semantic tokens are mode-paired, each pair is declared ONCE and evaluated in BOTH modes. Add `modes` to restrict. Add `debt: true` (or a mode array to scope it to one mode) to mark a known failure tracked in RECONCILIATION.md rather than fixed. As of v1 there are none.

$usage.body-text: 4.5:1 — normal body copy. NOTE: weight 600 does NOT qualify for the large-text exemption; only bold (700) does.
$usage.ui-boundary: 3.0:1 — WCAG 1.4.11 non-text: controls, focus rings, meaningful borders
$usage.decorative: exempt — measured and reported, never failed

DECORATIVE FILLS ONLY — chip backgrounds, icon tiles, chart bands. Exempt because a mark never carries meaning alone: a chip always has a label, an icon tile always has a glyph. Anything that CONVEYS meaning, including a chart line, must use the ink role instead.

RECLASSIFIED, not ignored. WCAG 1.4.11 applies to a visual indicator only where that presentation is ESSENTIAL to identifying the state. Selection here is carried by three simultaneous signals — a tinted fill, this border, and a trailing check glyph (verified on Figma node 1:222) — so the border is reinforcement, not the sole affordance, and the 3:1 threshold does not apply to it. If a future selected state ever drops the fill or the check, this must revert to ui-boundary and the tint must be strengthened.
The standard 13% tint background.

EXEMPT by specification, not by choice. WCAG 1.4.3 explicitly excludes text that is part of an INACTIVE user interface component from the contrast minimum. Deliberately still measured and reported so the value cannot drift unnoticed. Figma node 1:96 is the only reference for this state.

GRADIENT BACKDROPS NEED BOTH ENDPOINTS DECLARED. Only the flat-surface pairs were declared at first, so this card went unaudited — and its light mode was reusing the dark gradient's deep-indigo start behind near-black text at 1.58:1, the worst contrast in the system.
The binding constraint: secondary text at the gradient start is what set the palest usable light start value.
